gaps.title: Post-acquisition mandate to expand into new crops and new geographies at once
gaps.detail: AgroStar didn't acquire INI Farms to keep doing what it already did -- it explicitly said it's expanding into onions and vegetables, entirely new crop categories, while pushing into EU and North America markets INI Farms hadn't served before. More crops, more farmers, more geographies, all needing the same temperature-controlled handling pomegranates and bananas already require. Scaling a cold chain into new categories is exactly where consistency breaks down without one system tracking every crop and every farm the same way.
gaps.based_on: AgroStar... announced complete acquisition (100%) of... INI Farms... 'We will now target the entire F&V basket in terms of crops. In terms of markets, we would focus on the EU and North America primarily.'... 'start with the export of onions and vegetables and include more crops in future.'

gaps.title: Farm-gate temperature control across 2,000+ farmers in five states
gaps.detail: Sourcing spans over 2,000 contracted farmers across five states plus INI's own farms, covering roughly 5,500 acres. Fruit quality is set at the moment of harvest -- if temperature control doesn't start consistently at the farm gate across that many separate growers, no amount of downstream cold chain can fully recover it.
gaps.based_on: It works with over 2,000 farmers in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka for pomegranates and bananas, covering nearly 5,000 acres... farms spread over 550 acres in four locations in Maharashtra and three in Madhya Pradesh.

pitch.angle: AgroStar didn't just buy INI Farms to keep doing what it already does -- it explicitly said it's expanding into onions and vegetables, entirely new crop categories, while pushing into EU and North America markets INI Farms didn't serve before. That's more crops, more farmers, more geographies, all needing the same temperature-controlled handling that pomegranates and bananas already require -- scaling a cold chain into new categories is exactly where consistency breaks down without one system tracking every crop and every farm the same way. GND's ThinxFresh gives INI Farms that consistency from day one of the expansion, not after the first shipment goes wrong.
pitch.opener: As you expand from pomegranates and bananas into onions and vegetables for EU and North America, how are you keeping temperature-chain consistency across crops that didn't exist in your network a year ago?
